# Limits proposal, 18 October 2026 — a PROPOSAL, nothing here is in force

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/limits-proposal.mjs` from tests/limits-proposal-table.ts. Do not edit by hand: tests/limits-proposal.test.ts fails when this file is stale. -->

No limit in code is changed by this document. It answers one question for the owner: under the aligned receiving model (lib/receiving-costs.ts, docs/margin-alignment-2026-10-18.md), what is the smallest set of cuts to the PRINTED limits (visits, orders, video hours, storage, AI drafts and answers, emails) that would bring each base plan to 60% net at the sizing reading, every allowance used in full, the commission counted as zero? Prices, the number of plans and every hidden limit stay as they are.

## How the cuts are chosen

Lines are cut in this order, each down to at most 10% of today's figure (never below one hour of video or half a GiB of storage) before the next one is touched, and the last one only as far as needed: AI drafts / answers a month → Video hours watched a month → Storage → Orders a month → Store emails a month → Access emails a month → List emails a month → Visits a month. First come the lines a store is least likely to reach in full and where competitors give less or nothing (AI on entry plans, video watched, storage); then orders and the emails that go with them; then list emails and visits, which competitors give far more generously or do not limit at all. A proposed figure is rounded down to two significant figures (storage to half a GiB, video to whole hours) and the plan is computed again at the rounded figures. Each line's cost is linear in its figure; only storage's share of what a store keeps after its plan ends is taken off with it, so the proposal never counts on a saving it cannot show.

## Store assistant: the input cap that would keep 60%

Today each reply may send the model 24,576 bytes (lib/store-assistant-rules.ts, ASSISTANT_INPUT_BYTES), of which 16,384 are the store's facts; the add-on keeps 59.06%. The 700 replies a month, the price and everything else stay.

| Input cap | Of which the store's facts | About how many of the 40 products read, at today's average of 410 bytes each | Net |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 24,576 (today) | 16,384 | 40 | 59.06% |
| 16,304 (the largest that keeps 60%) | 8,112 | 19 | 60.00% |
| 13,054 (the largest that keeps 60% with the add-on's 25¢ room, what assistantMeetsFloor asks) | 4,862 | 11 | 60.36% |

The conversation and the rules keep their share; only the catalog text shrinks, so a buyer asking about a product past the cut is told more products exist and is answered less well.

## AI captions: the price that would keep 60%

Today: 25¢ a minute for each language, never less than $2.00, against the service's 10¢ a minute a language and 10¢ more should it count the spoken language apart. At its worst over every length (1 to 240 minutes) and 1 to 3 languages, it keeps −30.50%. No minimum charge alone can fix it: at 25¢ a minute the longest video misses on its own (4.91% at 240 minutes in one language).

The lowest price per minute that keeps 60% on the longest video is $3.99 a minute a language, but so close to the edge that the minimum charge would have to be $850.00. A little higher, the minimum falls to something a page could print:

| Price a minute a language | Minimum charge that keeps every length at 60% |
| --- | --- |
| $3.99 | $850.00 |
| $4.50 | $95.00 |
| $5.00 | $55.75 |
| $6.00 | $32.00 |
| $8.00 | $24.50 |
| $10.00 | $20.75 |

Captions are on sale today: **no** — they are charged only to a store with an active subscription (lib/auto-captions.ts), and no subscription can be started while the plans are closed (PLANS_ON_SALE false, app/api/billing/checkout/route.ts). Withdrawing them until a price is decided changes nothing a customer has today.

## For the owner

- Every proposed figure is a cut to a limit the customer sees, which the owner ruled out on 18 October 2026; this document only shows what it would take. Nothing is in force and nothing opens a sale.
- The cuts are deep because receiving a payment and using a plan in full already take more than the 17.24% of revenue the floor leaves after a 27.5% tax; the alternatives remain a price change or a cheaper way to receive payments.
